title: Bleyer's band at the Empire Ballroom and night walks
summary: Trying to date the Empire Ballroom job, he recalls carrying his trumpet up to 53rd Street at 3 a.m. and wandering Harlem.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: 1930, Archie Bleyer, I was still in college when Archie got a job at the Enpire Ballroom--Empire. There's a ballroom on 53rd and Broadway, it's no longer there. They used to have elevated tracks there. What was the name of it? It really doesn't make any difference.
Wait a minute, that had to be even later. I was in college then, so that period with Archie Bleyer must have gone on some time.
According to Chilton's, you said work with Archie Bleyer in 1932.

Then came Columbia and I went back to Archie with the band. '33 it must have been as well, and it must have been in '33 in that ballroom. I used to trudge up all the way to 53rd Street with the trumpet case at three in the morning, alone, nobody was around.
No, the IRT was very much there, I just did it.
No, I wouldn't recommend it, especially with a horn.
We used to do it, and also all through the thirties we used to wander around through Harlem and nobody ever

did anything.

I don't know if it was because of our youth or there was a different attitude in those days. Harlem was quite a tourist attraction then.

We'll go up to 1934 and '35, I had played summers with the kid band I was telling you about.
